subject: Re: Infrastructure canvas + routing story for our on-prem VPC deploy
messages:
From: Alicia Brennan <alicia.b@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-12T16:18:00Z
Subject: Initial ask: on-prem deployment constraints and diagrams

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks again for taking a look at our on‑prem requirements. Attached is a short packet with what we consider the minimal constraints for our deployment: physical rack demarcation, N-ACL expectations, routing adjacency with our transit fabric, and a short note on compliance evidence we will need during the security review.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood support a split control/data plane with an outbound-only control channel to your hosted control plane (we'd prefer outbound TLS from our side)?
- We need clear reference schematics for cable demarc, NAT/ingress points, and an egress policy that prevents uncontrolled third-party traffic.
- KMS/HSM integration: we will want details for customer key ownership and HSM-backed signing for CRL rotation.

We'd like a short readout and one annotated schematic we can hand to our colo ops team. Any known blockers (eg. required inbound control ports) please call out.

Attachments:
- acme-deploy-requirements.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks,
Alicia Brennan
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
alicia.b@acme.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Brennan <alicia.b@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-12T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Infrastructure canvas + routing story for our on-prem VPC deploy

Hi Alicia — thanks for the packet, and apologies for the slightly longer reply. I pulled together an early pass and a couple of artifacts for your colo team. Quick summary up front, followed by an attachment list and action items.

Executive summary:
- Redwood can support a split control/data plane for private deployments. The recommended pattern (attached) is:
  * Control plane agents run in a small, outbound-only management subnet in your VPC/colo. They initiate TLS to Redwood control endpoints (no inbound control ports required).
  * Data plane runtime (inference nodes) are in segregated tenant pools with an egress-only NAT gateway for model downloads/metrics; we prefer explicit egress allow lists.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS via standard KMIP or cloud KMS integrations. For HSM-backed signing we have a documented handshake for key wrapping and rotation (see runbook-draft.md).
- Observability and audit: we can ship per-token and per-request metadata to your SIEM over a customer-configured egress collector; we also provide immutable audit logs surfaced in the console for compliance evidence.

Attachments I uploaded for your team:
- rvw-schematic-v1.png (annotated diagram: cable demarc, mgmt subnet, data plane, egress NAT, monitoring tap)
- runbook-draft.md (draft: operations handoff + KMS/HSM integration checklist)

Callouts / constraints:
1) We strongly recommend a small management proxy that performs TLS termination for outbound control; this keeps ports closed inbound and simplifies firewall rules.
2) If you require an air‑gapped model (no downloads from public internet), we can support staged model shipment to a bucket inside your network and local ingestion, but that becomes an operational flow with a small manual step for each model release.
3) For SOC2 evidence we can supply: network diagrams, audit logs for a 90-day window by default, and key rotation history tied to KMS events. Extended retention is available as an add‑on.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30m call with your colo ops and our deployment lead (Karthik) to walk the schematic and confirm switch/rack handoffs.
- We will mark rvw-schematic-v1 as preliminary; after the call we can produce a vendor-ready wiring sheet.

Proposed times: Thu 2028-10-13 14:00 PT or Fri 2028-10-14 09:00 PT — which works for you?

Best,
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: rvw-schematic-v1.png (PNG, 1.2MB), runbook-draft.md (text, 4 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Irene / Alicia — quick operational notes from my side before the call.

Quoted for context:
> On 2028-10-12T20:05:00Z, Irene wrote:
> > The recommended pattern is: Control plane agents run in a small, outbound-only management subnet...

Operational additions:
- Canary / rollout: we recommend a two-stage rollout for early traffic: (1) a single dedicated inference pool (small GPU footprint) with canary routing for 5% traffic, (2) expand to full tenant pool after performance verification. We'll include batching config examples in the runbook.
- Firewall NAT: ensure the management subnet can reach these two FQDNs over TLS: ctl.redwood-inference.com and metrics.redwood-inference.com — we only need outbound 443. If your infra requires IP allowlisting, tell us and we will provide the current IP set and a signed notice for changes.
- Service accounts / certs: we'll issue short-lived certs for control agents by default; if you prefer HSM-backed cert signing, we need to coordinate your CA operator.

Irene — I'll take the wiring sheet template and populate port/MTU and suggested SNAT rules ahead of the call.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Dedicated Deployments | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

I've uploaded the requirements packet to the shared Drive folder and attached the invite. We will include our colo ops (James Park) on the call — I'll add him to the thread after I send the invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the call.

Alicia
